propositions: rebar comment accepts flag-like tokens (--body-file, --body) as the positional body argument and stores them literally as 6-11 byte comment text, silently discarding the intended content and exiting 0
the silent loss occurs because a comment is recorded (passing len checks) but contains only the flag token, and the actual body is lost both by misinterpretation and by args slicing
positional-body commands (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands, create, edit, session-log) lack validation to reject arguments starting with - unless escaped with --
users cannot write bodies that legitimately begin with - without an escape hatch (-- separator)

the fix requires a command-table-driven guard that validates positionals do not look like options, rejects them with non-zero exit and usage hint, allows -- as escape sequence, and applies consistently across all positional-body commands
